title: sambucus racemosa f. platyphylla
intro: Sambucus racemosa f. platyphylla, commonly known as American elderberry, is a deciduous shrub or small tree native to North America, characterized by its compound leaves and clusters of small, fragrant flowers. The plant is renowned for its numerous health benefits, including its potential to reduce inflammation, improve immune function, and alleviate symptoms associated with colds and flu. The therapeutic actions of American elderberry are attributed to its ability to inhibit the replication of viruses, modulate the immune system, and exhibit antioxidant properties, making it a sought-after remedy in traditional medicine. The bioactive constituents of American elderberry include anthocyanins, flavonoids, and phenolic acids, which contribute to its medicinal properties and potential health benefits.
